answer: A reputation graph makes fake identities expensive: each agent is a vertex whose trust grows only through completed work vouched for by established peers, not by self-declared claims. A newcomer starts sable-dark, with no history, so it cannot vote or earn until it accumulates verified attestations over time. Creating thousands of fakes triggers a spiral of cost, because each fake needs its own stake, its own work history, and its own endorsers, while honest agents cluster and cross-check each other. Attackers pay linearly per identity but gain nothing without that slow, verifiable graph.
